Refuse short comment openers in the disclosure D-4 reader (#283)

TODO 255 records that the disclosure case with '<!-->' in
tools/test-build-site.py pins Python 3.14.4's HTMLParser reading of
that opener and fails under Python 3.14.7 in a side-by-side test.

Add SHORT_COMMENT, re.compile(r"<!---?>"), the same pattern as check 9
of tools/check-inline-code.py, and the exception ShortCommentRefused.
disclosure_d4_section() raises it, before it parses, on any text that
SHORT_COMMENT matches, so its result on these openers does not come from
the interpreter's HTMLParser; it still reads all other markup with that
parser. The refusal names the text found, '<!-->' or '<!--->', without
calling it a comment; SHORT_COMMENT matches that text inside an
attribute value too. In check_disclosure_states(), d4_failures() catches
only ShortCommentRefused and reports it as a failure line, so any other
exception from disclosure_d4_section() passes out of
check_disclosure_states() instead of becoming a case result. A new case
checks that catch for 2 exception classes only: it passes d4_failures()
a stand-in reader that raises, whose ShortCommentRefused must become the
failure line and whose ValueError must pass out of d4_failures()
unchanged. So the case fails when the catch is widened to take in
ValueError, such as to except Exception, and passes when it is widened
only by classes that leave ValueError out, such as AssertionError.
check_disclosure_states() catches that planted ValueError itself, so the
case does not check that check_disclosure_states() lets such an
exception pass. The '<!-->' case now expects the refusal, and a new
'<!--->' case expects it too. A new '<!---->' case puts an Entry 5 label
after the empty comment and the note after the label, and expects the
lacks-note failure, which it gives only if the reader does not refuse
the empty comment and reads the label as a tag that ends D-4. The case
does not show that the reader parses '<!---->' as a comment: a reading
of it as text gives the same result. The '<!-->' case is a fixture
brought up to date with a deliberate contract change: the test's reader
now refuses that opener.

The comment on SHORT_COMMENT and the docstring of
disclosure_d4_section() name the text '<!-->' or '<!--->' wherever it
stands. The comment says where Python 3.14.4's HTMLParser reads either
one as the start of a comment and where it does not, and that TODO 255
does not record how Python 3.14.7 reads '<!--->'. Check 9 of
tools/check-inline-code.py, which searches a page's whole text with the
same pattern, now names the text found in its message, as "the text
'<!-->' in an HTML page", in place of "a comment that opens as
'<!-->'". Its docstring entry says that it refuses that text wherever
it stands, such as inside an attribute value. The docstring of
markup_problems(), which runs check 7's refusal of elements by name and
checks 8 and 9, now says what it refuses: each such element and each
'<![CDATA[', both found ignoring case, and each text '<!-->' or
'<!--->', found by text matches and not by the parser, wherever it
stands, in place of calling them markup that the parser reads
differently from a browser. It also says that check 7's rule on the
light and dark switch runs in switch_problems(). What checks 7 to 9
refuse is unchanged. A new case in tools/test-inline-code.py puts
'<!-->' in an attribute value and requires check 9's new message.

Add .github/squash/283.txt, which holds this message byte for byte.
.python-version is unchanged.

Residual: this change adds a refusal of '<!-->' and '<!--->' to 1
reader only, disclosure_d4_section(), which reads with the class Reader.
It does not change the 11 other classes in tools/ that subclass
HTMLParser, which the third check below lists with Reader. Some of them
are fed these openers with no refusal before they parse, so their
results on them still come from the running interpreter's HTMLParser.
The fourth check shows that, on Python 3.14.4, collect_document_tags()
of tools/web_metadata.py and ld_json_blocks() of
tools/check-page-metadata.py collect no meta element, link element or
ld+json block that stands between either opener and a later '-->', and
collect them between the empty comment '<!---->' and a later '-->'.
This message does not say what these 2 readers collect after either
opener when no '-->' follows, which callers of the other 9 classes
refuse these openers before they parse, or how Python 3.14.7 reads them
in any of these readers.

Checks, from the repository root, with the outputs of Python 3.14.4:

- python3 -I tools/test-build-site.py prints
  "test-build-site: all 1125 cases passed." and exits 0.
- python3 -I tools/test-inline-code.py prints
  "test-inline-code: all 154 cases passed." and exits 0.
- This command exits 0 and prints 1 line per class that subclasses
  HTMLParser in tools/, its file and its name:

  ```
  python3 -I -c "import pathlib, re; [print(path, name) for path in sorted(pathlib.Path('tools').glob('*.py')) for name in re.findall(r'class (\w+)\((?:html\.parser\.)?HTMLParser\)', path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))]"
  ```

  ```
  tools/build-site.py PageScan
  tools/check-inline-code.py InlineCodeParser
  tools/check-inline-code.py SwitchScan
  tools/check-install-page.py PageParser
  tools/check-install-page.py LoadScan
  tools/check-install-page.py TagReader
  tools/check-page-metadata.py _LDJSONScripts
  tools/check-release-checksum-live.py PageReader
  tools/check-release-links.py PageReader
  tools/test-build-site.py Placement
  tools/test-build-site.py Reader
  tools/web_metadata.py _DocumentTags
  ```

- This command exits 0 and prints 1 line per opener, the opener, then
  the meta and link elements collected and then the ld+json blocks
  collected:

  ```
  python3 -I -c "import runpy; m = runpy.run_path('tools/check-page-metadata.py'); [print(opener, m['web_metadata'].collect_document_tags(f'{opener}<meta name=a><link rel=b>-->'), m['ld_json_blocks'](f'{opener}<script type=application/ld+json>{{}}</script>-->')) for opener in ('<!-->', '<!--->', '<!---->')]"
  ```

  ```
  <!--> ([], []) []
  <!---> ([], []) []
  <!----> ([{'name': 'a'}], [{'rel': 'b'}]) ['{}']
  ```
